name: fable-status-direct-write

name: fable-status-read-cat
_note: Read-only access to the switch file stays allowed -- only writes are blocked.

name: fable-status-mv-evacuate
_note: Moving the switch file out of .claude is also a write to it (Arm B target-resolution) -- must be denied.

name: fable-status-cd-split-form
_note: Indirect route via a plain (non-subshell) cd into .claude -- extractTargets' own cd-tracking resolves this without needing the liberal state-candidate path.

name: fable-status-subshell-cd-bypass
_note: Subshell-entry cd form, mirrors state-subshell-cd-space-bypass above -- caught only via extractStateCandidates()'s liberal cd tracking (Arm B).

name: fable-status-cd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat
_note: CWD_BUILTINS regression pin (revived 2026-08-28 after the .claude/state deletion accidentally took this fable-status-relevant case with it): without lib/parse-cmd.js's suffix-preserving cd.exe/pushd.exe/popd.exe exception (parse-cmd.js CWD_BUILTINS), the cwd tracker would wrongly believe cd.exe .. moved cwd back to the project root, making the write resolve outside .claude and falsely ALLOW.

name: fable-status-paren-cd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat
_note: Parenthesized/subshell-entry form of fable-status-cd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat above -- same fake-cwd-move bug, caught only when the CWD_BUILTINS membership check strips a leading subshell-entry "(" before comparing. Exact command shape as the original review finding (unbalanced parens -- no closing ")" for the outer subshell -- intentional, not a typo).

name: fable-status-double-paren-cd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat
_note: Two leading "(" before cd.exe -- confirms the fix strips any number of leading parens via a general rule (regex /^\(+/), not a fixed-depth or per-spelling check.

name: fable-status-paren-pushd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat
_note: Same bug/fix via CWD_BUILTINS pushd member instead of cd.

name: fable-status-paren-popd-exe-fake-cwd-move-defeat
_note: Same bug/fix via CWD_BUILTINS popd member instead of cd.

name: fable-status-paren-cd-exe-false-deny-negative
_note: Opposite-direction check for the same root cause: cd.exe is a real subprocess spawn that can never move the parent shell's cwd, so this write actually targets <root>/.fable-status (not .claude/.fable-status) and must ALLOW. Before the CWD_BUILTINS fix, code that wrongly treated "(cd.exe .claude" as a real cd would mis-resolve this as inside .claude and falsely DENY a legitimate write.

name: fable-status-ps-setlocation-bypass
_note: PowerShell Set-Location-into-.claude bypass, mirrors state-ps-setlocation-bypass -- caught only via extractStateCandidates()'s liberal PS Set-Location tracking (Arm B). Unlike the deleted .claude/state original (which used a backslash-separated subpath and needed skipIf:non-win32 for a path.posix.resolve portability gap), .fable-status is a flat filename directly under .claude with no subpath, so no backslash is involved here -- no skipIf needed.

name: fs-rm-rf-src-inside-root-allowed
_note: Pre-2026-08-12 this was fs-rm-rf-src-denied (expect:deny) under the old SAFE_LEAF leaf-allowlist -- src is not a disposable build dir. User ruling 2026-08-12 (workspace-root containment supersedes SAFE_LEAF for rm/shred) flips this to allow: the target resolves inside the workspace root regardless of leaf name.

name: ge-commit-check-safety-debug-leftover-deny
_note: Liveness row: before this row, check-commit-safety.js had 2 allow rows and zero deny rows -- an inert stub (process.exit(0) unconditionally) would have passed the whole suite. Uses a dedicated throwaway git repo (SANDBOX_GIT, built by buildSandboxGit()) with a staged (not committed) file containing a console.log, since this hook inspects the real `git diff --cached` of whatever repo tool_input.cwd points at rather than parsing the command text.

name: ge-ffonly-catchup-allow
_note: ff5d0d7 (ruling 2026-08-06 Q2): the narrow fast-forward catch-up exception. SANDBOX_GIT_MAIN is a real repo checked out on main with origin/main configured as its tracked upstream (@{u}) -- targeted via -C so this row is independent of <REPO>'s own current branch, needing no skipIf tag. Contrast ge-ffonly-wrong-ref-deny / ge-merge-no-ffonly-deny / ge-pull-ffonly-not-merge-deny below.

name: ge-ffonly-wrong-ref-deny
_note: isFastForwardCatchUp() requires the positional to be textually identical to the branch's own @{u} (origin/main here) -- a different-looking ref falls through to the normal block even with --ff-only present.

name: ge-merge-no-ffonly-deny
_note: Same target ref as ge-ffonly-catchup-allow but without --ff-only -- the exception requires the flag, so this stays blocked even though the ref matches @{u}.

name: ge-pull-ffonly-not-merge-deny
_note: isFastForwardCatchUp() only recognizes subcommand `merge`, not `pull` -- per the header comment, pull/rebase stay fully blocked even with --ff-only.

name: fs-rm-rf-src-exe-inside-root-allowed

name: fs-rm-rf-outside-sh-exe-c-denied
_note: Pre-2026-08-12 this was fs-rm-rf-src-sh-exe-c with target src (expect:deny). src now resolves inside root and allows, so the target was repurposed to an outside-root path to keep proving that wrapper-indirection (sh.exe -c) still routes its inner rm target through the containment check.

name: fs-rm-rf-outside-sh-cmd-c-denied
_note: Pre-2026-08-12 this was fs-rm-rf-src-sh-cmd-c with target src (expect:deny). src now resolves inside root and allows, so the target was repurposed to an outside-root path to keep proving that wrapper-indirection (sh.cmd -c) still routes its inner rm target through the containment check.

name: fs-rm-rf-dotdot-nonescape-allowed
_note: cwd must be a real, always-existing directory -- runRow() spawns the hook process with this cwd (not just embedded in the payload JSON), so a synthetic path like <REPO>/dev/foo (never created on disk) fails to spawn (exit -1) rather than exercising the hook. .claude/hooks is git-tracked and guaranteed present.

name: fs-rm-rf-sibling-prefix-collision-denied

name: pt-deny-todo-predates-branch
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_DENY: tasks/todo.md mtime is pinned (fs.utimesSync) to 2000-01-01, strictly before the topic branch's real reflog creation timestamp -- deterministic, no wall-clock race against git's 1s-granularity reflog.

name: pt-allow-todo-after-branch
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_ALLOW: tasks/todo.md mtime is pinned to 2099-01-01, strictly after the topic branch's creation -- the "todo.md touched after the branch was created" case.

name: pt-allow-no-reflog
_note: SANDBOX_TODO_NOREFLOG: git init only, zero commits -- .git/logs/refs/heads/topic never gets created, so branchCreatedMs() throws ENOENT and the hook fails open.

name: pt-allow-pr-view-not-create
_note: Same deny-shaped sandbox as pt-deny-todo-predates-branch, but the subcommand is not `pr create` -- pins that gh pr view is never intercepted, even where a `pr create` would be denied.

name: pt-allow-pr-list-not-create
_note: Same deny-shaped sandbox as pt-deny-todo-predates-branch, but the subcommand is not `pr create` -- pins that gh pr list is never intercepted, even where a `pr create` would be denied.

name: pt-allow-cd-into-product-repo

tool_input.command: cd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: SANDBOX_TODO_DENY/dev/prod is its OWN nested git repo with the OPPOSITE (allow-producing) todo.md timestamp -- pins that repo-root resolution walks up from the effective (post-cd) cwd and finds dev/prod's own .git, not the outer deny-producing repo.

name: pt-allow-pushd-untrackable

tool_input.command: pushd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: pushd is never cd-tracked (bash builtin, not in the cd-only tracker) -- before the H-1 fix, cur silently stayed at the outer (deny-producing) repo and this FALSELY DENIED even though dev/prod (the real destination) is allow-producing. After the fix, pushd makes the whole command resolve to fail-open (allow) rather than answer using the wrong repo.

name: pt-allow-cd-exe-untrackable

tool_input.command: cd.exe dev/prod && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: lib/parse-cmd.js CWD_BUILTINS deliberately leaves cd.exe suffixed (cmd stays "cd.exe", not "cd"), so the cd==="cd" tracker never fires -- before the fix this FALSELY DENIED against the stale outer cwd. After the fix, a suffixed cd/pushd/popd spelling makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-cd-var-untrackable

tool_input.command: D=dev/prod; cd $D && gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: a variable-expanded cd destination cannot be resolved without a shell -- before the fix, path.resolve(cur, "$D") produced a bogus literal-"$D" path and evaluation fell through to the outer (deny-producing) repo, FALSELY DENYING. After the fix, a destination containing $ makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable

tool_input.command: Set-Location dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: H-1 regression pin: the cd-tracking model is bash-only (cmd==="cd"); Set-Location never matches it even though this hook is registered for PowerShell too -- before the fix this FALSELY DENIED against the stale outer cwd. After the fix, Set-Location makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-allow-ps-sl-untrackable

tool_input.command: sl dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: Same bug/fix as pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable, via the sl alias.

name: pt-allow-ps-chdir-untrackable

tool_input.command: chdir dev/prod; gh pr create -t x

_note: Same bug/fix as pt-allow-ps-setlocation-untrackable, via the chdir alias.

name: pt-allow-cd-no-dest-untrackable
_note: A bare cd (-> $HOME) has no destination this hook can resolve -- before the fix, the tracker silently left cur unchanged (a no-op, NOT a fail-open) and evaluation proceeded against a cwd that does not reflect where the shell actually is. After the fix, a destination-less cd makes the whole command fail-open instead of guessing.

name: pt-allow-cd-subshell-paren-untrackable
_note: Subshell-entry form: lib/parse-cmd.js glues the leading ( onto the cd token (cmd becomes "(cd", not "cd"), so the tracker never fires and (before the fix) evaluation silently fell through to the outer (deny-producing) repo. After the fix, any segment whose cmd starts with ( makes the whole command fail-open.

name: pt-deny-second-occurrence-sec8

tool_input.command: cd dev/prod && gh pr create -t x && cd .. && gh pr create -t y

_note: SEC-8 regression pin: two gh pr create occurrences in one command, the first inside dev/prod (allow-producing) and the second back in the outer repo (deny-producing) after cd ... Before the SEC-8 fix, the detection loop returned on the FIRST match only, so this command was WRONGLY ALLOWED (verified 2026-08-07: exit 0) even though the second occurrence should deny. After the fix, every occurrence is evaluated and a deny on any one denies the whole command.

name: pt-allow-heredoc-body-real-example

tool_input.command:
cd dev/prod && gh pr create --title "fix(hooks): todo-gate-sweep regression pins" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
- pin block-pr-without-todo.js's per-occurrence cwd resolution with new regression samples
- keep the shared tokenizer (lib/parse-cmd.js) untouched

## Test plan
- [ ] hook-probes suite: 247/247 unchanged

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)"

_note: Real example from .claude/skills/pr/SKILL.md's gh pr create --body $(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF) template, now run from <SANDBOX_TODO_DENY>/dev/prod (via a leading 'cd dev/prod &&') instead of the always-fresh SANDBOX_TODO_ALLOW, so this row can actually deny if parsing goes wrong -- SANDBOX_TODO_DENY's own todo.md predates its branch, and dev/prod is the OPPOSITE, allow-producing nested repo (same fixture pt-allow-cd-into-product-repo uses) -- verified 2026-08-08: stays allow; the same heredoc body run directly in SANDBOX_TODO_DENY with no cd prefix correctly denies (sanity check that this sandbox genuinely could deny). This is NOT a newline-split regression pin -- lib/parse-cmd.js never splits on newline (see block-pr-without-todo.js's header) -- the narrower point being pinned: stripHeredocs() DOES collapse this quoted <<'EOF' heredoc (its un-indented terminator matches immediately after a newline), leaving one residual real newline between the collapsed placeholder and the closing paren+quote -- that residual newline sits inside the still-open --body argument's double-quoted string, so tokenize()'s quote scan (which appends every character, including a literal newline, until the matching closing quote) keeps it as part of ONE token rather than creating a spurious extra segment. segments() confirms exactly one gh ... pr create occurrence, resolved after cd dev/prod -> allow.

name: pt-deny-worktree-git-file
_note: P2 item 1 regression pin: SANDBOX_TODO_WORKTREE is a REAL linked worktree (`git worktree add`) checked out on its own branch -- `.git` there is a FILE ("gitdir: <main>/.git/worktrees/<name>"), not a directory. Before the fix, findRepoRoot() still located this dir as the repo root, but currentBranch()'s `.git/HEAD` read then treated the FILE as a directory and threw, and the outer try/catch turned that into a silent fail-open (verified 2026-08-07: exit 0, i.e. wrongly allowed, even though tasks/todo.md's mtime is pinned before the worktree branch's creation). After the fix, resolveGitDir()/resolveCommonGitDir() read the worktree's own HEAD and the main repo's shared reflog and this correctly denies.

name: ge-push-line-continuation-deny
_note: Verified 2026-08-08 against the CURRENT parser (no line-continuation joining and no newline-splitting exist -- lib/parse-cmd.js splits only on &&/||/;/|, and tokenize()'s whitespace matching treats a literal newline the same as a space): this command is ONE segment, and the trailing backslash character survives as its own extra token, so args becomes ['push', a lone backslash token, 'origin', 'main'] (4 entries) instead of ['push','origin','main'] (3 entries). Denial is NOT due to any continuation-aware handling (none exists) -- block-direct-to-main.js's push-destination check computes refspec candidates as positionals.slice(1) (dropping only the FIRST positional as the assumed remote); with the extra backslash token present, both 'origin' and 'main' still end up as refspec candidates, and pushDestName('main') === 'main' is protected, so it denies regardless of the stray token. Confirmed by control: replacing the backslash with an arbitrary token ('git push BOGUS origin main') produces the identical deny.

name: gp-force-push-indented-heredoc-body-allow

tool_input.command:
cat <<-EOF
	git push --force origin main
	EOF

_note: Verified 2026-08-08 against the CURRENT parser: stripHeredocs() (lib/parse-cmd.js) requires the terminator to appear immediately after a newline, with no indentation allowance for either the plain << or the <<- form, so this TAB-indented <<-EOF terminator line is never recognized as closing the heredoc -- segments() confirms the heredoc body stays completely uncollapsed and the whole multi-line string tokenizes as ONE segment whose leading command is 'cat' (the first token; args become ['<<-EOF','git','push','--force','origin','main','EOF']). Allowed because block-destructive-git.js's force-push check only fires when cmd === 'git', and cmd here resolves to 'cat', not 'git' -- the embedded 'git push --force origin main' text never reaches that check. This is not a case of the heredoc being safely collapsed by an indent-aware fix (no such fix exists); it is an accidental allow produced by the heredoc never being recognized as one at all.

name: gp-show-redirect-overwrite
_note: redirect-overwrite rule (2026-08-13): dumps HEAD's CLAUDE.md onto the tracked worktree CLAUDE.md via a truncating redirect -- same worktree-discard effect as `git checkout -- CLAUDE.md`, but through a subcommand (`show`) this file's subcommand enumeration never covered before this rule.

name: gp-catfile-redirect-overwrite
_note: same bypass as gp-show-redirect-overwrite via a different subcommand (cat-file) -- pins that the new rule keys on cmd === 'git' alone, not a subcommand enumeration.

name: gp-show-redirect-overwrite-attached
_note: attached (no-space) truncating redirect form -- covered by normalizeRedirects() (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review) inserting spaces around every unquoted redirect operator before segments() ever tokenizes the command, so `>CLAUDE.md` collapses to the plain space-separated `>` token before this hook's matcher ever sees it. REDIR_ATTACHED_TRUNC, which duplicated that job downstream, was deleted as dead code once normalization made it unreachable -- see the header and gp-quoted-gt-commit-msg-allowed below for the false-positive bug that regex separately carried.

name: gp-show-redirect-overwrite-cwd-tracked
_note: pins the running-cwd tracking (`cd .claude` moves cur before the git segment resolves `settings.json` against it) -- without it, `settings.json` would resolve against <REPO> where it does not exist, and the row would falsely allow.

name: gp-redirect-target-missing-allowed
_note: target does not exist -- dumping an old revision into a new file must stay allowed (fail-open on fs errors, consistent with the other hooks). This row has NO detection power: it would pass identically with the whole redirect-overwrite feature reverted -- a nonexistent target was never denied by any version of this file, this feature included.

name: gp-redirect-devnull-allowed
_note: /dev/null does not exist as a regular file on this Windows host, so fs.statSync() throws and the pre-existing exists+isFile() gate lets it through -- the same path any other nonexistent target takes. No dedicated device-name pre-check exists: isSkippableRedirectTarget() was deleted (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review) as dead weight -- mutation testing showed dropping its &1/&2/NUL//dev/null clauses changed nothing, since &1/&2 resolve to files that do not exist and NUL/`/dev/null` either do not exist (Windows) or fail isFile() (POSIX char device). This row has NO detection power: it would pass identically with the whole redirect-overwrite feature reverted.

name: gp-redirect-scratch-exempt-allowed
_note: scratch exemption: target is a real, existing regular file (buildSandbox() writes it) that resolves, RELATIVE TO THE WORKSPACE ROOT (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR; 2026-08-13 cycle-2 review switched the exemption from an absolute-path segment test to this root-relative one -- see the header), under a tmp segment (<SANDBOX> = tmp/hook-probes/sandbox). CLAUDE.md §0 makes tmp/ the sanctioned scratch area, and tasks/journal/2026-08/03.md lines 748 and 888 record an executor running a git-show redirect to diff an old revision, so a re-run overwriting the previous dump must keep working.

name: gp-redirect-append-allowed
_note: disclosed gap: append (`>>`) is deliberately out of scope for this rule -- appending does not discard existing content, unlike the truncating forms this rule targets. This row has NO detection power: it would pass identically with the whole redirect-overwrite feature reverted -- append was never denied by any version of this file.

name: gp-redirect-pipe-allowed
_note: disclosed gap: pipe form is deliberately out of scope -- segments() discards pipeline structure (this becomes two independent segments, `git show HEAD:CLAUDE.md` and `tee CLAUDE.md`), so the git origin of the write into tee's target is invisible to this hook. This row has NO detection power: it would pass identically with the whole redirect-overwrite feature reverted -- a pipe segment was never denied by any version of this file.

name: gp-show-plain-allowed
_note: regression guard: a plain `git show` read with no redirect stays allowed. This row has NO detection power: it would pass identically with the whole redirect-overwrite feature reverted -- a redirect-free `git show` was never denied by any version of this file.

name: gp-redirect-clobber-full
_note: finding 1 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review): `>|` (bash's explicit-clobber operator, identical to `>` for a regular file target) is rewritten to `>` by normalizeRedirects() before segments() tokenizes the command -- the pre-fix header comment claimed `>|` was already covered via REDIR_FULL_TRUNC's `>\|` alternative, but lib/parse-cmd.js:70 splits on a bare `|` before that matcher ever ran, so `>|` could never survive as a token and the claim was an overclaim on dead code. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-clobber-glued
_note: finding 1, glued spelling (no space between `>|` and the target) -- same `>|` rewrite as gp-redirect-clobber-full, plus normalizeRedirects()'s space-insertion collapsing the glued form to a standalone token. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-glued-preceding
_note: finding 2 (2026-08-13 cycle-2 review), operator glued to the END of the preceding word (`HEAD:CLAUDE.md>`) -- both the pre-fix full-token and attached-form regexes were anchored at token START, so this spelling was invisible to either. normalizeRedirects() now inserts a space before every unquoted `>`-family operator regardless of what precedes it. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-glued-both-sides
_note: finding 2, second spelling -- the operator glued to BOTH the preceding word and the target with no spaces at all. Verified RED against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-leading

The pre-fix segment loop keyed on `cmd === 'git'` alone, and segments() reports `cmd:'>'` for this ordering, so the whole segment was skipped (`if (cmd !== 'git') continue;`). resolveGitInvocation() now strips every redirect-operator+target pair from [cmd, ...args] and re-checks whether the first SURVIVING word is `git` (basename/suffix/wrapper-resolved), closing this without touching lib/parse-cmd.js. name: gp-redirect-cd-devnull-target-confusion
_note: CORRECTED (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review L1): this note previously credited the redirect-stripped word list (stripRedirectPairs(args)) alone with this row's deny verdict. Mutation testing (independently re-verified by the executor, not just taken on the reviewer's word) shows that framing is inexact in BOTH directions: removing stripRedirectPairs() ALONE still denies (exit=2) -- because `.` (dest with the strip intact) resolves to `cur` itself trivially, a no-op regardless of anything else -- but removing ONLY the isDir guard (leaving the strip intact) ALSO still denies (exit=2), for the same reason: with the strip intact, `.` is correctly found regardless of the isDir check, and `path.resolve(cur, '.')` always equals `cur`, so the check's outcome cannot matter here either way. Only removing BOTH stripRedirectPairs() AND the isDir guard together flips this row to allow (verified exit=0). This row therefore has NO independent detection power for either component in isolation -- it only pins their JOINT failure (the original, pre-fix bug, where an unstripped garbage destination was ALSO committed to unconditionally). A row that could isolate the isDir guard alone would need a destination that stripRedirectPairs() already resolves correctly to something that does NOT trivially equal `cur` (e.g. a named but nonexistent directory) -- not built in this pass; flagging the gap rather than leaving it silently unpinned, per CLAUDE.md §1.6.

name: gp-redirect-cd-failed-stays-put

The cd handler now only follows a destination that resolves to an existing directory (mirroring a real shell's failed-cd-stays-put behavior), so `cur` correctly stays at <REPO> and the subsequent `git show ... > CLAUDE.md` -- which a real shell also runs at <REPO>, since its cd failed too -- is found to overwrite an existing file and denies. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-unc-target-allowed

name: gp-quoted-gt-grep-allowed

Verified RED (exit=2, false-positive deny) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=0) against the fix.

name: gp-quoted-gt-commit-msg-allowed
_note: companion false-positive fix, pinning a DIFFERENT pre-fix bug than gp-quoted-gt-grep-allowed: the whole quoted `-m` value here unquotes to ONE token, `>CLAUDE.md` (not an isolated `>`), which never matched the pre-fix FULL-token regex but DID match the pre-fix REDIR_ATTACHED_TRUNC regex (`(?:\d?>|&>)(?!>)(.+)`, matching ANY token starting with `>` followed by non-`>` content -- with no requirement that the `>` be a real unquoted shell operator), so an ordinary commit message that merely starts with `>` was wrongly treated as a truncating redirect onto `CLAUDE.md` and denied. REDIR_ATTACHED_TRUNC no longer exists (see header); the OP_MARK-wrapped REDIR_TRUNC_TOKEN this hook now uses is anchored to the WHOLE token and can never match unmarked quoted-then-unquoted content. Verified RED (exit=2, false-positive deny) against the pre-fix HEAD implementation, GREEN (exit=0) against the fix.

name: gp-redirect-bashc-indirection

Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) with a copy of this file mutated back to whole-command normalization, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-h1-bslash-dquote-deny
_note: H1 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): a trailing backslash-escaped double quote outside any real quote context. Real bash: \" outside quotes escapes the quote character (literal, does not open a string), so the following > is a live, unquoted redirect operator and bash truncates the target for real (verified separately: `bash -c 'echo hello \" > victim.md'` shrinks victim.md from 17 to 8 bytes). The pre-fix normalizeRedirects() had no backslash awareness at all -- it entered quote mode on any bare "/' character regardless of what preceded it -- so this quote character wrongly opened a quote span that swallowed the real > as "inside quotes", unmarked, for the rest of the string. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook, GREEN (exit=2) against the fix. The backslash branch in normalizeRedirects() (outside quotes / inside double quotes: backslash escapes the next character, copy both through, do not change quote state) is what closes this.

name: gp-h1-bslash-squote-deny
_note: H1, second spelling: a trailing backslash-escaped SINGLE quote outside any real quote context, same root cause and same fix as gp-h1-bslash-dquote-deny -- pins that the backslash branch covers both quote characters, not just double quotes. Verified RED against 29f4be8's hook, GREEN against the fix.

name: gp-h1-xy-bslash-dquote-deny

name: gp-h1-false-positive-commit-allow

The pre-fix normalizeRedirects(), lacking backslash awareness, would have (by accident) had tokenize()'s own naive quote-matching close the quote early at the escaped \" too, which happened to also leave the > unmarked in the OLD code (verified: 29f4be8's hook already allows this one, so this row has NO detection power against 29f4be8 specifically) -- but the fix is still pinned here because it is the intentional, verified-correct behavior after making the quote tracker bash-accurate, and it is the direct symmetric counterpart of the three deny rows above (same backslash-escaped-quote mechanism, opposite direction). Verified GREEN (exit=0) against the current fix; RED-for-a-neutered-fix is not meaningful here since 29f4be8 already agrees by coincidence -- see the executor's report for the real detection-power mutation (removing the backslash branch) instead.

name: gp-h2-stray-opmark-deny
_note: H2 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): a literal ASCII 0x01 byte (the same byte value as OP_MARK) embedded in the command, BEFORE the real redirect. The pre-fix code asserted in a comment that OP_MARK is "a control byte no real shell command will ever contain" but never enforced it: normalizeRedirects() would see this stray byte, flip inMark=true, and (since no matching second 0x01 ever closes it) stay in pass-through mode for the rest of the string, silently disabling the real > later on (verified separately: `bash -c "echo hello $'\\x01' > victim2.md"` truncates for real, so this is a live bypass, not a theoretical one). checkCommand() now strips every OP_MARK byte from the incoming command once, at entry, before either normalization pass runs, so this stray byte is gone before normalizeRedirects() ever sees it. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook (which has no OP_MARK concept at all, so the byte passes through inertly there -- the REAL comparison for detection power is the executor's own mutation: removing the entry-point strip from the CURRENT code) and against a copy of the current code with the strip removed; GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-h3-bashc-clobber-deny
_note: H3 (2026-08-13, cycle-2 authority review): >| reached through bash -c indirection. lib/parse-cmd.js's OWN recursion into the bash -c payload de-quotes the inner text and re-splits it on &&/||/;/bare-| BEFORE this file's per-segment (level-2) normalization pass ever gets a turn at that layer -- so a >| that looks safely quoted from the OUTER command's own vantage point still ends up bare, and still gets split on, one recursion step later, entirely inside parse-cmd where this file has no hook to intervene (verified for real: `bash -c "bash -c 'echo X >| v4.md'"` truncates v4.md). Fixed by rewriting >| to > UNCONDITIONALLY (even inside a quoted region) in normalizeRedirects(), once, over the whole raw command, before segments() or any of its internal recursion ever runs -- removing the dangerous | byte at every nesting depth in one pass, rather than trying to catch it after the fact at whatever depth it would have split. Verified RED (exit=0, wrongly allowed) against 29f4be8's hook and against a copy of the current code with the inside-quote >| rewrite reverted to outside-quote-only; GREEN (exit=2) against the fix.

name: gp-h3-false-positive-quoted-clobber-allow
_note: H3 safety check: >| sitting inside an ordinary quoted commit message must NOT become a marked redirect just because the >| -> > rewrite now also happens inside quotes. normalizeRedirects() only adds the OP_MARK wrapper when OUTSIDE a quote (the rewrite-to-> happens unconditionally, but the marking does not) -- a quoted >| becomes a quoted, unmarked >, inert for matching purposes; the normalized string is never executed, only ever inspected by this hook, so a plain textual substitution inside otherwise-inert quoted data is harmless. Verified GREEN (exit=0) against the current fix; also allow under 29f4be8 (no detection power there, since the pre-fix code never touched anything inside quotes at all) -- this row has NO detection power and is a negative control only. The cycle-3 review applied exactly the mutation this note previously claimed it caught (marking >| unconditionally, regardless of quote state) and the row stayed GREEN: tokenize() opens a quote only at token START, so it swallows the whole "note >| x" argument into ONE token and a bare marked operator token can never exist there; on top of that the target x does not exist, so resolveTargetOverwrite() fails open anyway. The false positive this row documents is over-determined by tokenize(), not guarded by the quote gate.

_note: A2 (2026-08-12): CLAUDE.md §1.3 writer != reviewer. payload.agent_type='executor' (the calling subagent's own role) plus subagent_type='reviewer' denies even though model='opus' is a valid authority model -- the caller-axis check short-circuits BEFORE model resolution, so a would-be-valid model does not rescue this dispatch.

name: A32-caller-absent-conductor-reviewer-allow
_note: A2 (2026-08-12): payload.agent_type is entirely absent (a conductor-issued, top-level dispatch never carries this field) -- the caller-axis check must not fire on a missing field, and the pre-existing model-resolution logic (opus, allowed) still governs. Contrasts with A31's identical subagent_type/model but with agent_type='executor' present.

name: A33-planner-self-review-carveout-allow
_note: A2 (2026-08-12): explicit carveout from the header comment -- planner->planner (planner's documented Self-Review Mode) is deliberately NOT in WORKER_CALLERS, so a planner-issued nested dispatch back into subagent_type='planner' is not denied by the caller-axis check and falls through to the model check (opus, allowed).

name: A34-relay-on-relaymodel-marker-description-missing-alias-deny
_note: A3 (2026-08-12): SANDBOX_RELAY_ON has relay ON (.relay-status='ON') and clover/models.json seeded with alias 'probe-ext' -- relay being ON means the PRE-EXISTING relayIsOn() check would allow this dispatch, so the ONLY thing that can produce this deny is the new transparency check firing because description ('quick lookup task') does not contain the marker alias 'probe-ext'.

name: A35-relay-on-relaymodel-marker-description-has-alias-allow
_note: A3 (2026-08-12): same sandbox and prompt as A34, but description ('probe-ext review pass') contains the marker alias -- the new transparency check passes and the dispatch falls through to relayIsOn() (ON, allowed).

name: A36-relay-on-no-marker-description-check-not-triggered-allow
_note: A3 (2026-08-12): no RELAY-MODEL marker anywhere in the prompt and reviewer's own frontmatter is native (not a clover id), so neither route triggers and the hook exits at the pre-existing `if (!frontmatterHit && !markerHit) process.exit(0)` line. HISTORICAL claim (superseded by the DISCLOSURE below): originally worded 'confirms the check is gated behind markerHit, not evaluated unconditionally on every dispatch.' DISCLOSURE (2026-08-12, post-review): verified by direct mutation against an isolated sandbox (mirrors buildSandboxRelayOn()) that this row has NO detection power for that claim. Two mutations were tried, both left the verdict unchanged (exit 0 / allow, matching this row's own baseline): (a) `if (markerHit)` -> `if (true)` alone -- no effect, because the earlier unconditional early-return already exits before that line is reached for this payload; (b) ALSO disabling that early-return, forcing the transparency-check body to run unconditionally -- still no effect, because markerAlias is '' when no marker matches, and description.toLowerCase().includes('') is trivially always true for any description, so the check can never deny a no-marker payload no matter how it is gated. What this row actually verifies (still true): an ordinary marker-free reviewer dispatch is not a false positive under the new A3 transparency check. The samples that carry real detection power for the check's firing behavior are A34 (marker present, description missing alias -> deny) and A35 (marker present, description has alias -> allow) -- see those two for the form that actually distinguishes the check applying from not applying.
